questions.q: A series LCR circuit is subjected to an ac signal of $200 \mathrm{~V}, 50 \mathrm{~Hz}$. If the voltage across the inductor $(\mathrm{L}=10 \mathrm{mH})$ is $31.4 \mathrm{~V}$, then the current in this circuit is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Voltage across inductor } \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{L}}=\mathrm{IX}_{\mathrm{L}} \\ & 31.4=\mathrm{I}[\mathrm{L} \omega] \\ & 31.4=\mathrm{I}[\mathrm{L}(2 \pi \mathrm{f})] \\ & 31.4=\mathrm{I}\left[10 \times 10^{-3}(2 \times 3.14) \times 50\right. \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=10 \mathrm{~A}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: When you walk through a metal detector carrying a metal object in your pocket, it raises an alarm. This phenomenon works on
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Metal detector works on the principle of transmitting an electromagnetic signal and analyses a return signal from the target. So it works on the principle of resonance in AC circuit.

When the LC circuit detects any resonating frequency from any metal which is near to it, electric field will be created which will lead to induces current in the coil and changes in the signal flow through the coil.

questions.q: A circuit element <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> when connected to an AC supply of peak voltage <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> gives a peak current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> which is in phase with the voltage. A second element <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math> when connected to the same AC supply also gives the same value of peak current which lags behind the voltage by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math> are connected in series to the same supply, what will be the rms value of the current in ampere?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As current is in phase with the applied voltage, element X should be resistive with R=V0I0=1005=20 Ω.

As current lags behind voltage by 90°, element Y should be inductive with XL=V0I0=1005=20 Ω

When X and Y are connector in series, 

Impedance, Z=XL2+R2=202+202=202 Ω

Now, peak current, I0=V0Z=100202=52 A

Thus, the rms value of current is Irms=I02=52 A

questions.q: A coil of negligible resistance is connected in series with $90 \Omega$ resistor across $120 \mathrm{~V}, 60 \mathrm{~Hz}$ supply. A voltmeter reads $36 \mathrm{~V}$ across resistance. Inductance of the coil is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 36=I_{\mathrm{rms}} \mathrm{R} \\ & 36=\frac{120}{\sqrt{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2+\mathrm{R}^2}} \times \mathrm{R} \\ & \mathrm{R}=90 \Omega \Rightarrow 36=\frac{120 \times 90}{\sqrt{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2+90^2}} \\ & \sqrt{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2+90^2}=300 \\ & \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2=81900 \\ & \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}=286.18 \\ & \omega \mathrm{L}=286.18 \\ & \mathrm{~L}=\frac{286.18}{376.8} \\ & \mathrm{~L}=0.76 \mathrm{H}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Given circuit is R-L growth circuit

The current is the circuit is given by, 

i=ER1-e-tτ

For current to be half of the peak value,

i=E2R=ER1-e-tτ

Solving t=τln2

t=LRln2=11000.693=0.00693≃7 ms

At time t=15 ms,

i15 ms=ER1-e-1510

⇒i=61001-14=34×6100=0.045 A

⇒U=12Li2

by solving we get U=1 mJ.

questions.q: A 110 V,50 Hz, AC source is connected in the circuit (as shown in figure). The current through the resistance 55 Ω, at resonance in the circuit, will be _____A.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let current in the inductance is iL, through the capacitor is iC and through resistance is iR at any instance as shown in the figure.

According to the Kirchoff's junction law, iR=iL+iC.

At resonance XC=XL hence iL=iC. Also, current through the capacitor and inductor have phase difference of π rad. Therefore, they will form destructive interference and hence the current through the resistance will be 0.

questions.q: A telegraph line of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math> has a capacity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>km</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and it carries an alternating current at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math> kilo cycle per second. If minimum impedance is required, then the value of the inductance that needs to be introduced in series is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mH</mi></math>. (If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>10</mn></msqrt></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The frequency given is 0.5 kilo cycle per second ⇒f=500 Hz⇒ω=2πf=1000π rad s-1.

Total capacitance of the wire is C=0.01×10-6×100 F.

Impedance is minimum at resonance. Therefore, for minimum impedance

XL=XC

⇒ωL=1ωC⇒L=1ω2C=110002×π2×0.01×10-6×100=10-1 H=100 mH

questions.q: For ac circuit shown in figure, $\mathrm{R}=100 \mathrm{k} \Omega$ and $\mathrm{C}=100 \mathrm{pF}$ and the phase difference between $\mathrm{V}_{\text {in }}$ and $\left(V_B-V_A\right)$ is $90^{\circ}$. The input signal frequency is $10^x \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec}$, where ' x ' is ______

$\theta+\theta=90^{\circ} ; \theta=45^{\circ}$
$\tan \theta=\frac{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}}{\mathrm{R}}$
$\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}=\mathrm{R} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{~W}_{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{R}$
$\mathrm{W}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{C}}}=\frac{1}{100 \times 10^3 \times 100 \times 10^{-12}}$
$=\frac{10^{12}}{10^7}=10^5$
